short: A boy emperor installed by his own father, and the last to hold the western imperial title.
full:
Romulus Augustulus was proclaimed western emperor on 31 October 475 CE by his father Orestes, a former secretary to Attila the Hun who had risen to command the western field army and deposed the previous emperor, Julius Nepos, in all but name. Still a child, Romulus held no real authority; his diminutive nickname, Augustulus, "little Augustus," reflected how little he mattered even to contemporaries.

When Orestes refused demands from the army's largely Germanic foederati for land grants in Italy, they rebelled under the officer Odoacer, killed Orestes, and deposed Romulus on 4 September 476 CE. Odoacer did not name a replacement emperor, instead sending the imperial regalia to Constantinople and ruling Italy himself as king, an act later historians took to mark the end of the western Roman Empire.
